root_idea.summary: The root centers on smallness, paucity, and having little.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to limited quantity or property, taking little, and being satisfied with little or turning away from something. Related Classical extensions concern scant water and estimating amounts.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form زَاهِدٌ.

senses.definition: Disinclined to something; not desiring it and willing to accept only little of it.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence uses the construction زَاهِدِينَ فِيهِ, describing people who were not interested in Joseph and accepted little for him. The sense can express either turning away from something or contentment with only a small amount of it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ascetic abstinence, especially from worldly pleasures; devotion expressed through religious service and devotional exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some usage distinguishes زَهَادَةٌ as abstinence concerning worldly matters and زُهْدٌ as abstinence in religion. In a religious application, it may involve taking only the minimum of a lawful thing and leaving the remainder to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abstinence in eating; eating little.
To restrict or straiten one's household through niggardliness or poverty.
To estimate or conjecturally compute an amount, measure, size, extent, or number, especially the produce of palm trees or the amount of property or livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage concerning palm trees and property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to abstain from, relinquish, shun, or become disinclined to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively with فِي or عَنْهُ; it is the causative counterpart of زَهِدَ فِيهِ or زَهِدَ عَنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impute niggardliness or stinginess to someone; to charge someone with being a miser.
To possess little property, so that one's possessions are not desired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person whose property is scant enough to attract no desire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a display of ascetic abstinence; to devote oneself to religious service or devotional exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may emphasize either the outward manifestation of asceticism or engagement in devotion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contemn or despise something, holding it in little or mean estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in plural constructions and applied to treating a matter or prescribed penalty as insignificant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon something little or of small account, including another person's gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of evaluating an object, amount, or gift as insignificant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small quantity; as much as is sufficient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression خُذْ زَهْدَ مَا يَكْفِيكَ, “take the small amount sufficient for you.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The poor-rate, or zakāt, regarded as the small portion due from property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical usage reported as an alternative designation for زَكَاةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land or small watercourses characterized by limited water-flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions vary: the land is explained either as flowing only after much rain or as flowing after the least rain. The expression زَهَادُ التِّلَاعِ refers to small watercourses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who eats little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, including in expressions such as زَهِيدُ الأَكْلِ and زَهِيدُ الطَّعْمِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small in quantity or number, especially a small gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an amount, number, or gift.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contemptible, paltry, mean, or niggardly; a person possessing or doing little good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe a thing as paltry or a person as low, ungenerous, narrow in disposition, or sordid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Content with little; not desirous of more.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction هُوَ زَهِيدُ العَيْنِ or لَهُ عَيْنٌ زَهِيدَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A narrow valley or tract of land that receives or releases little water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe a valley made to flow by only a slight quantity of water, or land from which little water comes forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who abstains, especially from worldly pleasures; an ascetic or devotee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle may describe general abstinence and, more particularly, a person engaged in religious devotion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person possessing little property, so that it is not desired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a believer or other person whose possessions are scant.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested once, as the plural active participle in 12:20. The additional entries are broader Classical Arabic usages and are not automatically Quranic attestations.
The geographical usage has variant descriptions of how little or readily water flows; these alternatives are preserved rather than resolved.
